la:adj:arvus.html:
arvus, a, um, adj.
for aruus from aro
.
That has been ploughed, but not yet sown, ploughed, arable: ager, arvus et arationes ab arando, Müll.: arvum, quod aratum nec dum satum est,; Paul. ex Müll.: aut arvus est ager aut consitus aut pascuus aut florens,: Non arvus hic, sed pascuus est ager,: agri arvi et arbusti et pascui lati atque uberes,.—Hence,
Subst.
arva, ae, f. (sc. terra), an arable field, cornfield; only twice, ante - class., Naev. ap. ; Pac. ib.—
arvum, i, n. (sc. solum), an arable field, cultivated land, a field, ploughed land, glebe (cf. Doed. Syn. III. p. 8; class.): nec scibat ferro molirier arva,; : sol lumine conserit arva,; cf. ; ; ; et saep.: ex arvo aeque magno,: prata et arva et pecudum greges diliguntur isto modo, quod fructus ex eis capiuntur,: arva non afferent cibum,: Numidae pabulo pecoris magis quam arvo student,: ne perconteris, fundus meus, optime Quincti, Arvo pascat erum, (i. e. frugibus: arvum autem ab arando dictum est, Crucq.): arva per annos mutant, et superest ager,; ; .—
Meton.
A region, country: Aspicis en praesens, quali jaceamus in arvo,.—
Poet., in gen., fields, plains, regions: arva putria, Liv. And. ap. Müll.: genus humanum multo fuit in arvis durius,; : nec pisces (queunt) vivere in arvis,: Circaea arva,: Peneïa,; so ; 15, 276; 11, 62; 11, 196; et saep.: pomosa,: quā tumidus rigat arva Nilus,; ; so, arva deserti,: arva pacis,.—Hence also,
For pascuum, pasture-ground: Arvaque mugitu sancite bovaria longo: Nobile erit Romae pascua vestra forum,i. e. the Forum Boarium at Rome,.—
Arva Neptunia, for the sea, (cf. : campi liquentes). —
Land, a shore, coast: jamque arva tenebant (angues),.

senses: an ancient city in Hispania Baetica

la:noun:arvina.html:
arvīna, ae, f.
Grease, fat, suet, lard.
In gen.: pinguis, * (secundum Suetonium arvina est durum pingue, quod est inter cutem et viscus, Serv.).—
Esp.
Of the victim in a sacrifice (eccl. Lat.), ; ; so the dim. arvinula, * .—
Of a person: de latere ejus arvina dependet,.—
Greasiness, fatness, in gen., ; .—
Arvīna, a surname of the dictator A. Cornelius Cossus, .

la:other:Arverni.html:
Arverni, ōrum, m., = Ἀρβερνοί, Plut.; Ἀρουερνοί, Strabo,
a people of Gaul, in the present Auvergne, ; ; ; ; cf. Mann. Gall. p. 130.— Hence, Arvernus, a, um, adj., Arvernian: Arvernum genus (vini),.
